messages.content:
The `addValue` method in the `Frequency` class allows adding a plain `Object` as a value, but it enforces that the added object must be comparable to the existing values. The method checks if the object is an instance of `Integer` and converts it to a `Long` before proceeding to add it to the frequency table. If the object is not comparable, a `ClassCastException` is caught and an `IllegalArgumentException` is thrown.

The bug report mentions that the first call to `addValue(Object)` should not allow adding a plain `Object`, it should only allow `Comparable` objects.

Based on the current implementation of the `addValue` method, the issue may be related to the implementation not correctly enforcing the restriction that the added object must be comparable to existing values. This could be the root cause of the first call allowing a plain `Object` to be added.

Next, I will investigate further to confirm the root cause and suggest a diagnosis.

This explains why the test is failing when it tries to add a plain `Object` without any exception being thrown.

To diagnose the issue further, I will inspect the `addValue` method and the relevant logic to understand why the restriction is not being enforced as intended.

Upon further examination of the `addValue` method in the `Frequency` class, it is clear that the method is designed to ensure that the added value must be comparable to existing entries. The implementation includes a check for whether the value is an instance of `Integer` and converts it to a `Long` to maintain compatibility.

The root cause of the issue where the test `testAddNonComparable` fails to throw a `ClassCastException` when adding a plain `Object` seems to be related to the logic in the `addValue` method not correctly enforcing the comparability requirement. It is possible that the comparability check logic is not covering all cases where an added object may not be comparable with existing values.

To fix this issue and resolve the bug, the logic in the `addValue` method should be reviewed and possibly adjusted to ensure that only `Comparable` objects can be added, rather than allowing plain `Object` instances. This adjustment will align the behavior with the intended design where non-comparable objects should not be allowed to be added.

Next, I will provide suggestions on where the fix should be applied in the codebase.
The issue can be addressed by modifying the logic in the `Frequency.addValue` method to correctly enforce the comparability requirement. To fix the bug, the following method should be adjusted:

```java
org.apache.commons.math.stat.Frequency.addValue(java.lang.Object)
```
